transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-22
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Ben Cho (Redwood SE), Emma Reyes (Lumina CFO), Marcus Li (Head of Eng), Priya Nair (Security Lead), Daniel Ortiz (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Quick security posture discovery; customer evaluating whether Redwood Hosted can meet compliance or whether Dedicated/Private needed. Action: share SOC2 and network diagrams, schedule technical deep dive.

00:00 Aisha (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Aisha, AE for Redwood, and with me is Ben, our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
00:10 Emma (Lumina): Hey, thanks, doing well. Quick background: we're Lumina Finance, we're building an ml-driven credit insights product, security is obviously critical. I'm Emma, CFO but I'm helping run vendor evaluation.
00:20 Marcus (Lumina): Marcus here, head of engineering. Priya and Daniel are our security and infra leads.
:32 Ben (Redwood SE): Great, hi all, excited to run through security posture. We'll go high-level then dig into specifics: SOC2, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention.
01:05 Priya (Lumina): We're particularly concerned about PII residency, log retention, and access control. We need to know if hosted is possible or if we must go Dedicated/Private to satisfy our regulators.
01:22 Aisha: Totally. Quick note — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant, we also have ISO cert in progress; I'll share artifacts after. Hosted customers can get isolation via dedicated model instances and strict data controls, but for full network isolation we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
01:45 Priya: When you say "isolation via dedicated model instances" can you clarify? Does that mean data never touches multi-tenant storage?
02:01 Ben: Sure. For Hosted we separate at the inference runtime level — requests are isolated, and payloads are ephemeral; we don't persist customer prompts beyond retention windows unless configured for logging. That said, the control plane is multi-tenant. If you need VPC peering and egress restrictions we recommend Dedicated or Private.
02:25 Daniel (Lumina SRE): Can you do VPC peering for Dedicated? We run in AWS in us-east-1 and need to ensure no cross-region replication.
02:40 Ben: Yes — Dedicated gives you customer-dedicated GPU pools in your region, with VPC peering and private subnets. Private gives you our control plane options to be customer-managed; on-prem air-gapped variants are available too.
03:05 Emma: What about audit logs? We need immutable logs for all admin actions and user token usage for at least seven years for some of our regulators.
03:20 Aisha: We provide audit logs and activity trails. For Hosted we retain audit logs per plan; for longer retention or immutable logs we can push to your S3/GCS, or integrate with your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). For Dedicated/Private you can control retention and export policies entirely.
03:42 Priya: Export to our S3 sounds promising. Are logs tamper-evident? Do you support WORM or object lock?
04:00 Ben: We support pushing logs to customer-managed buckets where you can enable S3 Object Lock/WORM. On Redwood side logs are write-once and we keep checksums, but for aggressive compliance customers we recommend direct export to your storage.
04:15 Priya: Ok. Encryption at rest and in transit?
04:23 Ben: All traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. At rest we use AES-256. For KMS: hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys, but we also support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or GCP KMS for Dedicated and Private, and HSM integrations for FIPS/HSM needs.
04:45 Marcus: Can you rotate keys on demand? What's the process?
04:52 Ben: Yes — we support key rotation. For customer-managed KMS rotation is governed by your key policies; for Redwood-managed keys we rotate on a schedule and provide attestations. If you need HSM-backed keys we can surface hardware-backed keys via our KMS integrations.
05:10 Emma: About SSO — we use SAML with SCIM provisioning. Can Redwood integrate with our IdP?
05:20 Aisha: Absolutely. We support SSO via SAML, OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, and SAML assertions with attribute mapping. We have SSO flows for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private you manage SSO in your env.
05:35 Priya: RBAC — how granular is permissioning? Can we do per-team model access and token scoping?
05:45 Ben: Yes. We have role-based access control with built-in roles and custom roles. You can scope tokens to endpoints, models, and rate limits. For Dedicated/Private you get tighter network and IAM integration with your existing IAM.
06:10 Daniel: Do you support short-lived credentials or just API keys?
06:17 Aisha: We support both. Short-lived tokens via OIDC flows and API keys. You can bind tokens to specific policies and rotate them.
06:30 Marcus: What about data retention for prompts and generated outputs? Our legal requires deletion after 90 days for PII unless otherwise stored.
06:40 Ben: By default Hosted retains ephemeral data for troubleshooting for up to 30 days and can be configured. We can set up longer or shorter retention windows; for Dedicated/Private you control retention completely and can enforce automatic purges. We'll need to capture your retention requirements to map to config.
07:05 Priya: Are there any telemetry or usage events that Leak PII to staff? Who can access logs?
07:15 Aisha: Access controls are strict. Access to raw logs is restricted to SREs on a need basis and audited. For Hosted customers we have internal controls and blinding options for logs. We also provide redactions for PII in logs if needed.
07:40 Emma: For SOC 2 evidence, do you provide the full report and the bridge letters?
07:48 Aisha: Yes — SOC 2 Type II report is shareable under NDA. We'll also provide our latest pen-test summary. I'll attach them to follow-up.
08:02 Marcus: If we go Dedicated, how's the onboarding? Network setup lead time?
08:12 Ben: Typically Dedicated onboarding is 2-4 weeks depending on network approvals. Private or on-prem can take longer. We'll provide a runbook and configuration checklist.
08:28 Daniel: Any limitations on model variants for Dedicated? We use quantized models and want latency guarantees.
08:36 Ben: We support common quantization profiles; latency SLOs are tunable and we expose batching/caching controls. For strict SLOs we can pin models to specific GPU types and reserve capacity.
09:01 Priya: Do you do penetration testing and vulnerability disclosures?
09:08 Aisha: Yes. We perform regular internal and external pen-tests and have a bug bounty program. We can share MRA or third-party test summaries under NDA.
09:22 Priya: Do you publish a data processing addendum and DPA?
09:27 Aisha: Yes — DPA, data flow diagrams, and standard contractual clauses available. We'll include the DPA in the follow-up.
09:40 Emma: About regulatory residency — we need all European PII to remain in eu-west-1. Can Redwood guarantee that in hosted?
09:50 Ben: In Hosted we route requests to region-based endpoints; we provide region pinning, but full guarantees for residency without Dedicated/Private are harder. For strict data residency you should consider Dedicated in the target region or Private. We can route inference in-region but control plane artifacts might be global. We'll detail exact flows in the data flow diagram.
10:18 Marcus: Any notable gotchas customers run into?
10:22 Ben: Biggest issues are retention defaults, accidental admin privileges, and not planning for key management. Also model drift and eval monitoring — we recommend integrating Redwood Optimize for quality monitoring.
10:40 Priya: On audit logs: do you log full request/response bodies? That's a no-go for us unless redacted.
10:50 Ben: We don't log full request/response by default for hosted; we log metadata and hashed fingerprints. If customers enable retention for debugging we can redact or push logs to your bucket where you control access.
11:10 Emma: If we start with Hosted for speed, what's the path to Dedicated? Is it seamless?
11:18 Aisha: It's fairly straightforward. We support lift-and-shift; you can pin model versions and migrate traffic with canary rollouts. There is some onboarding work for networking and capacity.
11:35 Daniel: For compliance, we'd like to do an in-person or screen-share review of network configs.
11:40 Ben: Sure — that's what the technical deep dive will cover. We'll prepare sample VPC setups and a runbook.
11:50 Priya: What about encryption key custody for logs vs model weights vs data?
12:00 Ben: Different tiers. Data at rest (customer data) can be under your KMS. Model weights (open-source or Redwood-verified) are encrypted at rest with our keys unless you bring your own model into Private deployment where you control keys. Logs can be pushed to customer KMS-managed buckets.
12:22 Emma: Any SLA differences across deployment modes?
12:28 Aisha: Hosted has a standard SLA for uptime and latency tiers; Dedicated has stronger, commitment-backed SLAs. Private is negotiated as part of the contract. We'll include the SLA matrix in the follow-up pack.
12:45 Marcus: Can you show us an example of audit logs export format? JSON/CEL?
12:52 Ben: We export structured JSON events compatible with SIEM ingestion (Splunk/Datadog). We'll share sample artifacts.
13:05 Emma: On the legal side: is Redwood willing to sign our data processing terms and specific recital for financial regs?
13:14 Aisha: We are typically flexible; we'll route legal to our privacy counsel. We'll need to review specific clauses.
13:30 Priya: One more — are there mechanisms for data subject requests and deletion workflows?
13:38 Ben: Yes. We have a data subject request workflow and can assist in automating deletion across logs and cached KV entries. For Hosted, we need to coordinate with our ops team; for Dedicated/Private you can implement automated deletion.
13:55 Emma: Ok that's helpful. Can you send the SOC2 and network diagrams after this?
14:00 Aisha: Yes, I'll send SOC2, DPA, pen-test summary, sample audit logs, and the Dedicated vs Private TCO sheet.
14:10 Marcus: We'll gather our retention and residency specifics and loop in procurement.
14:18 Priya: Also please include details about HSM/FIPS support.
14:25 Ben: Will do.
14:35 Aisha: Recap of next steps: we'll share docs, Ben will schedule deep dive, Lumina will confirm retention/residency, and we'll follow up on pricing and timelines.
14:50 Emma: Thanks all, that was productive.
15:00 End of call.
